description:
SIZED s399 (probe-first).  t/op/lexsub.t, 156 rows, TRANSPILE-FAIL today.

**The #314 note that this file "dies in Pl/Parser.pm 'Negative repeat count
does nothing'" is WRONG, measured s399** -- that is a WARNING printed ten
times, not the killer.  The killer is:

    Parser2 TODO: lexical 'x__file__2' possibly captured by nested sub etetetet
    rc = 2, zero output

i.e. the CAPTURE refusal (#314 family A-iv / the _promote_captured path), not
anything lexical-sub-specific.  The "Negative repeat count" warnings come from
`Pl/Parser.pm:8908`, `"  " x $self->indent_level` with a NEGATIVE indent level
-- an independent bookkeeping bug worth its own look (it means the emitter's
indent push/pop is unbalanced on this input).

WHAT WORKS ALREADY (probed s399 vs perl 5.40.3, scratchpad ls1.pl/ls2.pl):

    my sub f { "F" }              print f()          both: F
    { my sub g { "G1" } g() }     block-scoped       both: G1
    sub outer { my sub h {"H"} h() }                 both: H

So the SYNTAX parses and simple cases already run.  Two divergences found:

  * RECURSION through the lexical name: `my sub rec {... rec($n-1) ...}` --
    perl DIES "Undefined subroutine &main::rec called" (a `my sub` is not in
    scope inside its own body; that is what `state sub` is for), PCL returns
    "rrr".  PCL being more permissive on a program perl REJECTS is CLAUDE.md
    principle 9 territory, not a fix target -- but op/lexsub.t asserts the
    perl behaviour, so those rows will fail and need a not-supported line.
  * SCOPING IS BROKEN across scopes -- task #337: `my sub x` compiles to a
    PACKAGE sub, so two same-named lexical subs in different scopes clobber
    each other and every `\&x` resolves to the last one (perl `8 3`, PCL
    `3 3`, silent).  That is the substantive half of this file and it is
    already filed.

SIZE THE FILE AS TWO STEPS, in this order:
  1. #337 (the scoping) -- it is the real feature work, and it is what the
     4 failing rows in op/const-optree.t need too.
  2. Then the capture refusal above, which is what actually blocks this file
     from producing ANY rows.  Measure what op/lexsub.t scores once it
     transpiles BEFORE sizing step 3 -- the file also tests `state sub`,
     `our sub`, prototypes and attributes on lexical subs, and the reachable
     row count is unknown until it runs (the s396 lesson: "one refusal blocks
     N rows" is an upper bound until the file has run).

BAR: as #337 (name resolution ⇒ the full sweep is the gate).


MEASURED s410, and the answer is that the rows are NOT behind a lexsub bug.

After #376 (which fixed the three uncovered rename spellings and recovered 2
of the file's drops, 14 -> 12), t/op/lexsub.t alone reads:

    perl 156/0      PCL 7/10, then the file DIES at row 18
    row 18 = `is((h F), 4242, 'our sub symbol translation does not affect meth
              names')`  --  op/lexsub.t:91

`h F` is the INDIRECT-OBJECT method call: perl reads it as `F->h`.  PCL
compiles it to `(pl-h (pl-F))` and dies on the undefined `pl-F`.  **139 of
perl's 156 rows are behind that one statement.**  Filed as task #381 with both
probe directions (PCL AGREES with perl when a `sub F` exists -- both call
`h(F())` -- so perl's own discriminator, "is there a declared sub of that
name", is implementable here and is #266's callable classifier).

So #341 is CLOSED as a sizing: its payoff is real (139 rows) but it is #381's
to collect, sequenced with #372/#343.  #373 (the string-eval sub-capture
alist) stays a filler -- the plan said "only if #341's read shows rows behind
it", and the read shows they are behind #381.
subject: op/lexsub.t (156 rows): SIZED s399 — the blocker is the CAPTURE refusal, NOT the "Negative repeat count" warning #314 recorded; do #337 (my-sub scoping) first
